payload.counterexample: Seed a sixth compound mutant: a broker that, after restart reconciliation of a claimed-but-unacknowledged envelope, treats a second identical submission as NEW work instead of an idempotent duplicate - directly violating protocol.md's 'identical submissions for the same participant, kind, and round are idempotent even after the dialogue advances'. A validity-maximizing sequencer emits mostly fresh well-formed operations; the probability that a 500-operation run replays an identical submission immediately after a crash-restart at that exact seam is small, so the gate passes at >=80% validity, the mutant survives, and the layer is dropped for zero yield. A gate that instead REQUIRES a fixed fraction of protocol-meaningful adversarial operations (identical resubmission, stale-round submission, duplicate ack, conflicting submission, re-poll after lease expiry) drawn from the documented recovery vocabulary hits that seam reliably in the same budget.
evidence: protocol.md 'Delivery and recovery': identical submissions idempotent even after dialogue advances; stale rounds return no-state-change; conflicting second submissions fail closed; duplicate acknowledgement is safe; re-armed delivery is deduplicated by the exact relay - the documented recovery surface is adversarial-operation handling, which an all-valid operation stream never exercises.

claim-7060's own evidence lists the operation alphabet as 'submit/wait/restart/crash-at-boundary/unbind-rebind' - omitting the duplicate/stale/conflict operations that protocol.md treats as first-class recovery inputs, so the sequencer-value assessments were made over an incomplete alphabet.

Both the matrix mutant gate and the sequencer yield gate depend on the mutant corpus, yet no exchange claim prices its implementation; the named-failpoint mechanism (claim-aa04) is the natural low-cost carrier for it.
falsifiable_tests: Gate redefinition test: stage-3 admission requires the generated distribution to contain at least 25% protocol-meaningful adversarial operations (identical resubmission, stale-round submission, duplicate acknowledgement, conflicting submission, re-poll after expiry), with 'invalid' reserved for schema-garbage only; if the redefined gate is unimplementable inside the 2-day box, the original validity-only gate stands and this challenge's first arm dies.

Idempotency-violation mutant: add the resubmit-after-restart-of-claimed-envelope mutant to the shared corpus; if the deterministic matrix already kills it with a scripted pair, the compound-coverage argument for the sequencer weakens and claim-b36e's softened form weakens further; if only an adversarial-mix sequencer kills it, the gate redefinition is vindicated.

Mutant pricing test: implement all six mutants as inverted failpoint behaviors in at most one focused day inside the core cap; exceeding that validates the unpriced-work premortem and forces the cap or the gate to move.

Clock-seam test: the one-day inventory must name an injectable time source for every lease/wake window within the invasiveness cap, or explicitly record transaction class 6 as live-matrix-only coverage rather than dropping it silently.
payload.premortem: Six months out, three ways this plan failed: (1) The sequencer shipped gated on validity percentage, ran quiet, and was dropped; v0.21 recorded 'randomized coverage adds nothing' as evidence; a real duplicate-retry-after-crash defect later shipped in the class the sequencer never sampled. (2) The mutant corpus turned out to be unpriced work inside the hard 8-day cap - five deliberate broker defects each needing a patch mechanism and a suite run; the maintainer, out of budget, skipped the gate, and the matrix shipped self-confirming - the exact failure the gate existed to prevent. Mitigation exists and should be recorded: implement mutants as inverted failpoint behaviors (skip/duplicate/reorder at the already-named seams), bounding corpus cost at about one day. (3) Transaction class 6 (claim/wake lease recovery) silently dropped out of the matrix because lease expiry and the five-minute wake retry depend on wall-clock reads inside the broker; deterministic rows need an injectable time source, and if adding one exceeds the ~150-line invasiveness cap the inventory has no recorded fallback - the class disappears without any test failing.
payload.strongest_failure_mode: The stage-3 admission gate is miscalibrated in a way that can silently invert its own verdict. The merged plan admits the sequencer only at '>=80% valid generated operations', but protocol.md's recovery semantics exist overwhelmingly to handle ADVERSARIAL operations: identical resubmission after crash (idempotent), stale-round submissions (no-state-change), conflicting second submissions (fail closed), duplicate acknowledgements (safe), re-armed delivery after rebind (deduplicated). A generator tuned to maximize broker-accepted valid operations systematically under-samples exactly this class, so the sequencer can pass its validity gate, run quiet, get recorded as 'zero yield beyond the matrix', and be dropped as theater - while the compound defect class it was built to explore (adversarial-op x crash x restart interleavings) was never actually sampled. The v0.21 full-Option-A go/no-go then reads 'randomization found nothing' from evidence that measured the wrong operation distribution.

payload.executive_summary:
DECISION: v0.20 verification depth for the cross-runtime-council broker. All three participants converged on a staged hybrid anchored on Option B, then the mandatory convergence challenge produced two material revisions and one verified confirmation that are folded in below.

PLAN (challenge-revised): Stage 1 (2-4 focused days): extract the documented recovery invariants as reusable checkers scoped strictly to durable broker artifacts; add test-only named failpoints at the persistence seams (~150-line invasiveness cap, test-local wrapper fallback); emit an invariant coverage map assigning every documented invariant to either the artifact oracle or a named relay-level/live-matrix observation - exactly-once EXTERNAL relay delivery is asserted only via the live matrix, never from broker artifacts (unanimously rejected claim, confirmed by code inspection: relay dedup state is memory-only in opencode_delivery_registry.ts). Stage 2: a one-day recovery-window inventory booked as its own line item (including an injectable-time-source check for lease/wake windows), then a ~24-36-row deterministic crash matrix over six structural transaction classes, release-gated on killing the mutant corpus - mutants implemented as inverted failpoint behaviors (priced <=1 day), with at least one held-out mutant not known to the checker author. Stage 3 (max 2 days, after the core): a state-aware seeded stdlib sequencer whose admission gate was REVISED by challenge: the generated distribution must include >=25% protocol-meaningful adversarial operations (identical resubmission, stale-round submission, duplicate ack, conflicting submission, re-poll after expiry) - not merely >=80% valid operations, which would steer generation away from the broker's core recovery surface - plus a replayable trace and >=1 kill of a compound mutant the matrix cannot express; zero yield drops it without prejudice. Full Option A (property-based model, possible dependency) is deferred to a v0.21 go/no-go gated on pure-core extraction or a 2-day spike meeting three entry criteria, decided on recorded mutant-corpus evidence.

MATERIAL CHALLENGE FINDINGS SURFACED AT THE ROUND LIMIT: (1) Gate miscalibration - a validity-only sequencer gate under-samples the adversarial operations protocol.md's recovery semantics exist to handle, so a quiet sequencer could be dropped on evidence measuring the wrong distribution; revision above. (2) Cap-arithmetic contradiction - stage upper bounds (2-4 + 5-8 days) exceed the 8-day core cap, and the plan cannot simultaneously treat the cap as a deadline and the coverage claim as complete; the maintainer must pre-commit a rule: if the post-inventory 80th-percentile estimate exceeds 8 days, either extend the budget or explicitly narrow the assurance claim (deferred rows listed, never silently dropped). (3) Assurance substitution risk - reassigning delivery-once to the live matrix is only safe if the live-matrix run becomes a blocking release-checklist row; otherwise the one tier verifying the relay boundary goes silently dark.

SURVIVING DISAGREEMENTS: whether the seeded sequencer captures most of full Option A's marginal value (one reject at 0.9, two uncertain; resolved empirically by the shared mutant-corpus comparison); whether the matrix expansion fits 3-5 vs 5-8 focused days (all uncertain; resolved by the one-day inventory); whether compound-sequence coverage is a v0.20 necessity or a measured experiment (split accept/uncertain; practically resolved by the admission gate). None warrants a fourth round - each resolves only through scheduled work, not deliberation.

DECISION AUTHORITY: the maintainer ratifies the revised gate, the cap rule, the inventory's budget position, and the live-matrix checklist change.
payload.recommendation: Adopt the challenge-revised staged hybrid: durable-artifact invariant checkers + named failpoints + invariant coverage map (stage 1); one-day window inventory with clock-seam check, then the six-class deterministic crash matrix gated on killing the failpoint-implemented mutant corpus including one held-out mutant (stage 2, 8-focused-day core cap with a pre-committed overrun rule: extend budget or explicitly narrow the assurance claim); a 2-day state-aware seeded stdlib sequencer admitted only with >=25% protocol-adversarial operation mix, replayable traces, and >=1 unique compound-mutant kill (stage 3, stretch); exactly-once external delivery verified only by the live recovery matrix, which becomes a blocking release-checklist row; full Option A deferred to a v0.21 evidence-gated go/no-go (pure-core extraction or three-entry-criteria spike, judged on recorded corpus results). No fourth round: every open question has a scheduled empirical resolver.
rejected_alternatives: Pure Option A in v0.20: independent estimates of 15-30 focused days to 4-8 part-time weeks exceed a solo best-effort release budget; building a model before invariant checkers exist risks the vacuous-harness failure the brief names.
Pure Option B as the permanent end state: unanimously rejected - a finite human-enumerated matrix cannot exhaust compound recovery interleavings (restart-x-retry-x-rebind-x-supersession).

Adopting a property-testing dependency in v0.20: pinned-seed stdlib randomness satisfies determinism, reproduction, and dependency constraints; whether library-grade generation/shrinking is ever needed is deferred to the v0.21 evidence gate.

Phase-by-boundary combinatorial matrix: superseded by six structural transaction classes (~24-36 rows) covering each distinct persistence choreography without duplicating shared staged-outbox/audit-intent mechanics.

Validity-only stage-3 admission gate (>=80% valid operations alone): rejected by convergence challenge - it optimizes generation away from the duplicate/stale/conflicting operations that constitute the broker's documented recovery surface.
Artifact-only invariant formulation with scope-out of resistant invariants: rejected via counterexample and code inspection; replaced by explicit reassignment to the relay/live-matrix tier.
user_decisions: Ratify or amend the challenge-revised stage-3 admission gate: >=25% protocol-adversarial operation mix (with 'invalid' reserved for schema-garbage) replacing the validity-only criterion; if unimplementable inside the 2-day box, the validity-only gate stands per the recorded falsifiable test.

Pre-commit the cap rule before stage 2: if the post-inventory 80th-percentile estimate exceeds the 8-focused-day core cap, choose EITHER extending the budget OR narrowing the v0.20 assurance claim with an explicit deferred-row list - the plan may not claim both the cap and complete coverage.
Decide whether the one-day inventory is booked inside or on top of the 8-day core cap (the ambiguity was flagged by challenge; either answer is workable, silence is not).
Approve making the maintainer-run live recovery matrix a blocking row in the release checklist, since exactly-once external delivery assurance now lives entirely in that tier.

Confirm the v0.21 full-Option-A go/no-go procedure: pure-core extraction or the two-day spike meeting the three entry criteria (independent model transitions, bounded valid-operation generation, automatic minimal replay), judged against recorded mutant-corpus results.

No fourth exchange round is requested by any participant: every surviving disagreement carries a scheduled empirical resolver; authorize implementation sequencing at your discretion - this council output is planning input, not implementation authorization.
